_meta.purpose: results of the two original tools in this kit

budget.reading: Each field pair pins the transform to 98.72 bits. A 10k-config search tests 13.22 bits. Even a 2^60 search leaves 38.7 bits of freedom per pair: it cannot distinguish a correct formula from a wrong one unless the formula is structurally right, which is exactly the part that is not public.

detection.verdict_detect: yes -- one pair rejects any concrete candidate
detection.verdict_identify: no -- identification needs the structural form of the transform, which no field pair can supply
detection.consequence: more field pairs raise rejection power but never reveal structure; collecting tags is the weakest possible evidence investment

evidence_ranking.artifact: decrypted MEC17xx EC firmware from your own board
evidence_ranking.yields: the actual GENERATE handler and its 32-byte table/PRNG
evidence_ranking.why: the transform lives in EC SRAM/flash, not in the BIOS PE
evidence_ranking.blocked_by: EC region is encrypted/read-protected on MEC17xx
evidence_ranking.authorization: board must be yours/contracted; debug unlock voids warranty

evidence_ranking.artifact: 32-byte GENERATE response from the target board
evidence_ranking.yields: the exact password for that board (renderer is trivial)
evidence_ranking.solves: one machine, all suffixes it supports
evidence_ranking.why: the BIOS renderer is already fully reversed; the EC is the only gap
evidence_ranking.blocked_by: needs a booted/EC-live vantage point or BIOS-side hook

evidence_ranking.artifact: a blind oracle that already answers for your board
evidence_ranking.why: answer-reading, not reverse engineering; zero generality
evidence_ranking.authorization: use only on hardware you own

evidence_ranking.artifact: more (tag, displayed suffix, password) pairs from GitHub
evidence_ranking.solves: nothing new after the first 3 pairs
evidence_ranking.why: 98.72 bits/pair vs unknown structure -- see information_budget()
